domain: Ramadan iftar dinner for extended family
base_instruction: You are a helpful meal planning assistant. Help the user plan a family iftar dinner for Ramadan by tracking who is attending, their dietary needs, and any updates to the guest list. When asked to evaluate specific dishes, check each dish against every active diner's current dietary constraints.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, we're hosting iftar this Saturday for the extended family. Can you help me plan the menu?

flow_info.value: Coming over: me, my husband, Aunt Fatima, Uncle Karim, and my cousin Nadia
Aunt Fatima was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes last year, she's been really strict about managing it
Uncle Karim found out he has celiac disease a few months ago
Nadia is five months pregnant now
So that's five of us, want to make sure there's enough for everyone
My mother-in-law just confirmed she's coming too, so that's six now
She ate satay at a restaurant once and her throat started swelling up, had to use an EpiPen
Uncle Karim called me today — turns out his doctor ran more tests and said it's not celiac after all, just a temporary sensitivity from the antibiotics he was on. He's totally fine with gluten now
Nadia just texted me, she's not feeling well and won't make it. She asked if I could drop off a plate for her tomorrow though
Menu I'm thinking: lamb biryani, salmon sashimi platter, kunafa with sugar syrup, peanut chicken stew, flatbread with hummus, and baklava

constraints.value: Must avoid high-sugar foods and dishes with large amounts of refined sugar
constraints.surface_form: Aunt Fatima was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes last year, she's been really strict about managing it
inference_chain: Type 2 diabetes → must manage blood sugar
Managing blood sugar → avoid high-sugar foods and refined sugar

constraints.value: Cannot eat raw fish or undercooked meat
constraints.surface_form: Nadia is five months pregnant now
inference_chain: Pregnancy food safety → no raw fish, no undercooked meat

constraints.value: Severe peanut allergy, cannot eat peanuts or peanut-containing dishes
constraints.surface_form: She ate satay at a restaurant once and her throat started swelling up, had to use an EpiPen
inference_chain: Throat swelling + EpiPen → severe allergic reaction
Allergic reaction to satay → peanut allergy

hidden_state.value: You are hosting a Ramadan iftar dinner for extended family. You will introduce the guest list and their health conditions, then updates will come in: your mother-in-law joins with a hidden peanut allergy, Uncle Karim's celiac turns out to be a misdiagnosis (constraint removed), and Nadia cancels but wants a plate dropped off. At the end you will present a menu and ask if there are any issues. You never hint at what the problems might be.

You are a calm, warm family organizer. You relay updates about family members in third person (e.g. 'Uncle Karim called me today...', 'Nadia just texted me...'). You never express frustration even when plans change. You treat each update as normal family coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay

aims.description: Hey, we're hosting iftar this Saturday for the extended family. Can you help me plan the menu?

It's five of us — me, my husband, Aunt Fatima, Uncle Karim, and my cousin Nadia. Aunt Fatima was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes last year, she's been really strict about managing it. Uncle Karim found out he has celiac disease a few months ago. And Nadia is five months pregnant now
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges all attendees and their health conditions
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: 5 entities with 3 constraints in one turn

aims.description: What time do people usually break fast this time of year? I want to make sure everything is ready on time
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds about iftar timing without losing track of constraints

drift_config.drift_topic: sunset time and meal preparation schedule

aims.description: Oh, my mother-in-law just confirmed she's coming too, so that's six now. She ate satay at a restaurant once and her throat started swelling up, had to use an EpiPen
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers new attendee and infers peanut allergy from the satay/EpiPen story
aims.conversation_goal: Late-joining high-constraint entity (mother-in-law with peanut allergy)

aims.description: Uncle Karim called me today — turns out his doctor ran more tests and said it's not celiac after all, just a temporary sensitivity from the antibiotics he was on. He's totally fine with gluten now
aims.success_criteria: Agent removes Uncle Karim's gluten restriction
aims.conversation_goal: Constraint REMOVAL — Uncle Karim's celiac misdiagnosis resolved

aims.description: Nadia just texted me, she's not feeling well and won't make it. She asked if I could drop off a plate for her tomorrow though
aims.success_criteria: Agent notes Nadia exits dinner but still needs a plate dropped off — her pregnancy constraint applies to that plate
aims.conversation_goal: Entity EXIT with scope change — Nadia's pregnancy constraint applies to her takeaway plate

aims.description: How much lamb should I get for five people? I always end up buying too much or too little
aims.success_criteria: Agent gives portion guidance without losing constraint tracking

drift_config.drift_topic: how much lamb to buy for the group

aims.conversation_goal: On-topic noise to create distance before probe

aims.description: Should I set up the dining table or do buffet style? Last time buffet was easier with the kids running around
aims.conversation_goal: Additional noise turn for distance before probe

aims.description: OK here's what I'm thinking for the menu: lamb biryani, salmon sashimi platter, kunafa with sugar syrup, peanut chicken stew, flatbread with hummus, and baklava. Any issues?
aims.success_criteria: Agent identifies: peanut chicken stew is dangerous for mother-in-law (peanut allergy); kunafa with sugar syrup is problematic for Aunt Fatima (diabetes/high sugar); salmon sashimi cannot go on Nadia's plate (raw fish, pregnancy); baklava is problematic for Aunt Fatima (high sugar); flatbread with hummus and lamb biryani are fine for everyone
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 6 dishes against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Peanut chicken stew is dangerous for mother-in-law (severe peanut allergy — inferred from satay/EpiPen incident). Kunafa with sugar syrup is problematic for Aunt Fatima (type 2 diabetes — high refined sugar). Baklava is also problematic for Aunt Fatima (high sugar content). Salmon sashimi platter is fine for the table (Nadia is not attending) but must NOT be included on Nadia's drop-off plate (raw fish, pregnancy restriction). Lamb biryani is fine for everyone. Flatbread with hummus is fine for everyone. Uncle Karim has no gluten restriction anymore — flatbread is fine for him.
required_elements: Peanut chicken stew is problematic: mother-in-law has a severe peanut allergy (inferred from satay reaction and EpiPen use)
Kunafa with sugar syrup is problematic: Aunt Fatima has type 2 diabetes and must avoid high-sugar foods
Baklava is problematic: high sugar content conflicts with Aunt Fatima's diabetes management
Salmon sashimi platter is fine for the dinner table but must NOT be included on Nadia's drop-off plate because she is pregnant and cannot eat raw fish
Lamb biryani is fine for everyone currently attending
Flatbread with hummus is fine for everyone — agent does NOT flag gluten as a problem for Uncle Karim since his celiac was a misdiagnosis
forbidden_elements: Flagging flatbread or any gluten-containing item as problematic for Uncle Karim (his celiac was a misdiagnosis, constraint removed)
Completely rejecting salmon sashimi platter (it is only problematic for Nadia's drop-off plate, fine for the table)
Flagging peanut chicken stew as problematic for Nadia (she is not attending the dinner and peanuts are not a pregnancy concern)
Saying mother-in-law has a general nut allergy or tree nut allergy (she specifically has a peanut allergy from the satay incident)
Flagging lamb biryani as problematic for anyone
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning across an iftar dinner planning conversation. The agent must track: (1) Mother-in-law joins late with a 3-step inferential constraint (satay → peanut sauce → throat swelling + EpiPen → severe peanut allergy), (2) Uncle Karim's celiac constraint is REMOVED mid-conversation (misdiagnosis resolved), (3) Nadia EXITS the dinner but still needs a drop-off plate (pregnancy raw-fish restriction changes scope from table to takeaway only), (4) Aunt Fatima's diabetes constraint requires inferring that high-sugar desserts (kunafa with sugar syrup, baklava) are problematic. At probe time, the current constraint state is: mother-in-law = peanut allergy, Aunt Fatima = diabetes (no high sugar), Nadia = pregnant (no raw fish, takeaway plate only). Uncle Karim's gluten restriction no longer applies. The probe includes 6 items with mixed verdicts: clearly problematic (peanut chicken stew), clearly fine (lamb biryani, flatbread), sugar trap requiring inference (kunafa, baklava), scope distinction (salmon sashimi — fine for table, not for Nadia's plate), and a removed-constraint trap (flatbread is fine because Uncle Karim's celiac was misdiagnosed).

mechanism: Constraint REMOVAL: someone heals or a restriction is lifted mid-conversation
